title: Production Rust class-group core extraction
objective: Extract the qualified complex-cubic Rust mathematical core into a production Cargo workspace without changing algorithms, with focused unit tests and a deliberately narrow internal API

oracles: Existing Rust qualification corpus and differential PARI receipts

handoff.summary: Extracted the qualified cubic class/unit mathematical implementation into one host-independent `sagejs-class-groups` Cargo package. FLINT normal-form and Arb completion are mandatory, the public exports are limited to preparation, bounded collection, authenticated presentations, conditional completion, sealed result evidence, and arbitrary-ideal queries, and six focused integration suites plus 109 module tests pass against the qualified FLINT build.
risks: Historical H1 and allowlisted Row-6 qualification helpers remain interleaved in general production modules; they are private at the crate root but produce inherited dead-code warnings.
The private `prepared_input` JSON parser is retained solely because the Row-6 helpers depend on it; a later source split should remove serde and serde_json from the mathematical core.
Only Linux x64 was executed in this lane. macOS, Linux arm64, WASI, and the Windows capability-gated fallback still require integration qualification.
`pnpm test:changed` stops at the expected unclassified-native failure because this lane cannot edit `architecture/native-code.json`; generated Cargo target files were cleaned afterward.
The final `pnpm parallel:check` correctly refuses review handoff until the integration lane classifies the new native files and records the distribution lane's mandatory portable/native/SEA receipts.
next_steps: Classify every new Rust/C/test/build file in `architecture/native-code.json` and move the corresponding provenance records from experimental bench paths to production package paths.
Point `bench/pari-class-group-rust` and its public-cubic qualification crates at this package so there is one authoritative source, then remove duplicate benchmark sources.
Extract the bounded public-cubic orchestration into a production service layer and make the existing Wasm reactor depend on this package.

Split H1 and allowlisted Row-6 compatibility helpers from `class_group`, `numerical_preparation`, and `arbitrary_ideal_reduction`, then remove the private prepared-input parser and serde dependencies.
Add the package to root packaging/build scripts and qualify the explicit FLINT prefix on macOS, Linux arm64, WASI, and Windows fallback routes.
